clue.text: Decoration, a high honour, being presented after ceremony

indicators.note: the honour is placed following the ceremony word, so it comes second in the answer

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial splendour
OM is the Order of Merit, a high British honour

explanation.surface: A medal awarded at a grand ceremony is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decoration' suggests a medal, chiming with the honour, but it is the woolly ball on a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A woolly ball is an ornament sewn on hats and costumes.

clue.text: Puts fresh string around documents

explanation.surface: Someone restrings a bundle of papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as RE-CORDS it means ties with new cord; as one word, written accounts or files.

clue.text: Worrying emblem displayed above sporting arena

indicators.note: in a down clue the emblem's word sits on top of the arena's word

parts.note: a badge is an emblem worn to show membership
a ring is the arena for boxing or the circus

explanation.surface: A worrying logo hangs over a sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestering someone persistently is a form of harassing, a verb sense of worrying.

clue.text: Assault spy on the street

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another places it above, so first

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation

explanation.surface: An attack on a secret agent in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To attack or harass physically is a verb sense shared by both words.

clue.text: Style of dress to make one irritable

explanation.surface: A uniform that puts its wearer in a bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is LIVER-Y, like 'liverish': bilious and bad-tempered, as if one's liver were out of sorts.
explanation.definitionFit: A servant's uniform is a distinctive garb; liverish people are tetchy and bad-tempered.

clue.text: Resembling an erstwhile comedian in the same way

parts.note: to resemble is to be like something
Ernie Wise, half of the British double act Morecambe and Wise, now dead

explanation.surface: Someone resembles an old comic, and does things similarly.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernie Wise was the straight man of Morecambe and Wise, a much-loved British TV comedy duo.
explanation.definitionFit: Similarly or also is the adverbial sense, doing something in a matching manner.

clue.text: Recording shows only half the south American capital

indicators.note: keeping just half the capital's name means its front five letters are dropped

parts.note: Montevideo is the capital of Uruguay

explanation.surface: A film shows just part of a South American city.
explanation.definitionFit: A tape or film of moving pictures is a kind of recording.

clue.text: University's lessons

explanation.surface: A note about what a university teaches.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is an English university town, so 'University's' gives READING'S; church lessons are passages read aloud from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A university in Berkshire, England, plus its possessive; and passages of scripture recited at a service.

clue.text: Surgeon offers absurdly poor rate!

indicators.note: something done absurdly is done in a crazy way, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Complaining that a surgeon pays badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who performs operations is a surgeon by job description.

clue.text: With slippery road surface youngster goes into bridge

indicators.note: the youngster's word is placed inside the bridge's word

parts.note: a span is a bridge or the arch of one
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A child walks onto an icy bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A training area made deliberately slick so drivers can practise controlling skids.

clue.text: Publicity person no good? Supply a tip

parts.note: a PRO is a public relations officer

explanation.surface: A useless press officer is asked for a hint.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed spike, as on a fork, is a sharp end or point.

clue.text: Soon a wind will swirl in mountainous area

indicators.note: swirling stirs the letters of these words round into a new order

explanation.surface: A weather forecast for a hilly region.
explanation.walkthrough: Snowdonia is the mountainous national park in north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh national park dominated by peaks, a highland region.

clue.text: Final number to be put up

indicators.note: in a down clue putting a word up reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: The last figure goes on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum left after all deductions is the final amount.

clue.text: Read tome about middle-of-the-road politician

indicators.note: about here means around or in a different arrangement, signalling a reshuffle

explanation.surface: Studying a big book on centrist politics.
explanation.definitionFit: A centrist who avoids extremes is a political moderate.

clue.text: Nasty smell in home counties sluice

indicators.note: the smell's word goes inside the counties' abbreviation

parts.note: SE is the South East, where England's home counties around London lie
pong is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A drain in the suburbs is stinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The home counties are those surrounding London, in South East England.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash down with a soaked cloth is to swab or rinse, a verb sense of sluice.

clue.text: Fantastic clap given to a Conservative trying to calm things down

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly fanciful, so the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Tory gets wild applause while soothing tempers.
explanation.definitionFit: Appeasing or conciliatory behaviour aims to soothe anger.

clue.text: Not likely to be taken to the cleaners?

definitions.text: Not likely to be taken to the cleaners?

parts.words: Not likely to be taken to the cleaners?
parts.note: being taken to the cleaners means being swindled; read literally, a garment that can be laundered at home need not go to the dry cleaner

explanation.surface: Someone too canny to be swindled.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric that can be laundered in water needs no professional cleaning.

clue.text: Harry's horse

explanation.surface: A man named Harry owns a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name but is the verb to harass; read 'Harry's' as 'harry is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pester persistently is to badger; an old worn-out steed is also called this.

clue.text: Strenuous exercise could make Erica sob

indicators.note: the letters could be made into another word, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A tough workout could leave Erica in tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhythmic workouts that raise heart rate are energetic exercise.

clue.text: Set on when retreating

indicators.note: retreating goes backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: Fixing something in place while backing away.
explanation.definitionFit: To solidify or firm up, as jelly does, is to set.

clue.text: Georgia has a mania for rock music

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
a rage is a craze or mania

explanation.surface: A Georgian obsessed with rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw guitar-band rock named after rehearsals in suburban car sheds.

clue.text: Exploit a small court

parts.note: CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Taking advantage of a tiny tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed or feat is an exploit, as in an act of bravery.

clue.text: Disorder when grenade is thrown

indicators.note: throwing something scatters it, so the letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: Chaos when a bomb is lobbed.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw into confusion or madness is to disorder, both verbs.

clue.text: Famous American to rise very rapidly in Connecticut

indicators.note: the rising word is put inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: CT is the postal abbreviation for Connecticut
to rocket is to shoot up fast

explanation.surface: A celebrity's career takes off in New England.
explanation.definitionFit: Davy Crockett was a frontiersman and politician, a celebrated figure of the US.

clue.text: Recover without drug — you mean that?

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the recovery word surrounds the drug

parts.note: to rally is to recover strength
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Getting better without medication, incredulously questioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it carries its old sense of 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of surprise asks if the speaker is serious.

clue.text: Score? It's five less than what you see here!

definitions.text: It's five less than what you see here!

explanation.surface: Someone tallies points and notices a number.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is printed as 25, twenty-five; five less is twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is a group of twenty; and twenty-five minus five gives the same count.

clue.text: She's a tart — but deep!

parts.note: a girl's name that is also a deep moulded fruit dessert, so 'tart' is a pastry rather than an insult

explanation.surface: A woman is called a hussy, but a profound one.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name and a fruit pudding baked in a deep mould lined with bread or sponge.

clue.text: Ceremonies in which entitlements may get read out

indicators.note: reading out loud means we hear the word rather than see it

parts.note: rights are entitlements

explanation.surface: At formal rituals a list of privileges is recited.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritual observances such as religious ceremonies are formal acts.

clue.text: Rag holding that easel together

indicators.note: the words hold the letters inside them, spanning the gap

explanation.surface: A cloth keeps an artist's stand in one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To rag is British for to mock playfully, i.e. to taunt.

clue.text: Refuse to vote, getting a black mark

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a stain is a mark

explanation.surface: Declining to vote earns someone a black mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To withhold one's vote is to decline to vote at all.

clue.text: None left, OK?

explanation.surface: Asking if things are fine now everyone has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'None left' as 'all right': if nothing is on the left, everything is on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfactory or fine is the usual sense; also everything on the right, none on the left.

clue.text: Against most of the lines taken by America

indicators.note: most of a word means it loses its final letter

parts.note: a verse is lines of poetry
US is the United States

explanation.surface: Opposition to poetry being taken up by America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by' joins the pieces: the shortened verse is followed by America's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin preposition means opposing, as in a match listing.
